The working directory here is empty, so I can't inspect the actual `misc`/`utils` contents to tailor this precisely — I'll base the proposal on the description you gave. Here's a structure that separates by *purpose* rather than dumping everything by vague category:

```
config/
  templates/          # config templates currently in misc
scripts/
  migrations/         # one-off migration scripts
docs/
  compliance/         # archived compliance reports
  archive/meeting-notes/   # old meeting notes (or just delete if truly stale)
lib/ (or packages/shared/)
  <feature-name>/     # shared helpers used by 2+ services — one folder per cohesive concern
services/<service>/internal/  # helpers used by only ONE service move here, not into a shared folder
```

For `utils`, the fix is to break it up by what each helper actually does (e.g. `lib/strings/`, `lib/dates/`, `lib/http/`, `lib/validation/`) instead of one flat bag — a `utils` catch-all tends to regrow the same problem within a year.

Two judgment calls to make as you sort:
1. **Anything used by only one service** shouldn't live in a shared folder at all — move it into that service's own directory. This is usually the biggest offender in "shared helpers" folders.
2. **Meeting notes and old compliance reports** — confirm these are truly reference-only; if nobody's opened them in months, consider whether they belong in the repo at all vs. an external doc store, rather than just relocating them.

If you point me at the actual repo path (or paste `ls misc utils`), I can turn this into a concrete file-by-file move plan and the shell commands to do it.
